description.en: Ontology for automatic database tuning: workload, DBMS metadata, access structures (indexes and materialized views), tuning heuristics and their SHACL rules.

comment.en: Statement with subqueries: it is composed of other DML Statements.

A rule of a heuristic. When a SHACL rule has the same IRI as a Rule individual, the script runs it only if a heuristic that defines it is enabled and the rule itself is not disabled (isEnabled false).
Statement 'create hypothetical index ...'. Its SQL text is in hasDescription and the index it creates in creates.
Left operand, comparison operator and right operand.
Constant value used in a predicate (e.g. 5, 'EUROPE', date '1994-01-01').
Relator between the optimizer and the DML statement it plans.

label.en: DML Statement Execution Plan with Access Structure

comment.en: «Relator» in the figure. A plan that accesses at least one access structure (inferred from 'accesses').

Cost of keeping an index up to date in one INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE execution (Salles, 2002, section 4.5.1; Morelli, figure 3.5): CA = 2 x ceil(r / R x P) + c x r, subtracted from hypothetical and real indexes alike.
«Relator» in the figure; a subkind of the DML Statement Execution Plan relator kind. Plan estimated with the hypothetical access structures.

Bonus of a real index for one execution, read from the real plan (from the DBMS): +hasBonus if the real plan uses the index (Morelli, figure 3.4, line 9); -hasBonus if the statement originated the index but the real plan did not use it (Rule_RealIndex_UnusedPenalty, an extension to Morelli).
«Relator» in the figure; a subkind of the DML Statement Execution Plan relator kind. Plan over the real configuration.
Change that one DML statement execution makes to the accumulated benefit (hypothetical index) or to the accumulated bonus (real index) of one index. Explains the numbers to the DBA.
Two predicates joined by a logical connector (and/or).
Set of tables referenced by a basic query (TS in Agrawal et al., 2000, used by Weberling, section 3.1.1). Interesting when TS-Cost and TS-Weight reach the threshold C.
HyGainVM of one execution for one hypothetical materialized view: Cost(q) - HyCost, q the query or subquery of the execution compatible with the view (figure 17).

Benefit of a hypothetical index estimated from the plans of one execution of a statement that originates it: +(real plan total cost - hypothetical plan total cost) if the hypothetical plan uses the index, the same value negated otherwise. Not recorded while the index is real.
Real index.

label.en: Specification of index to be scanned

comment.en: EDR (Oliveira, table 4.3): disk space left for tuning, in pages; a view is materialized only if its hypothetical pages (CE) are fewer (393216 pages of 8 KB in figure 4.11).
Hypothetical or real index the record changes.
TS-Weight(T) = sum over those queries Qi of Cost(Qi) x sizeTables(T) / sizeTablesClause(Qi), table size = pages.
Table of the index (not in the figures).
GrF in Morelli, figure 4.4: 100 - (Ra / Ri) x 100, Ra = table tuples / index blocks now, Ri = hasInitialRatio.

Accumulated benefit of a hypothetical index: sum of its records. After its real index is removed it starts again from -hasEstimatedCreationCost and counts only the executions after the removal (Morelli, section 3.3).
HyCost (Weberling, section 3.1.2, after Hose et al.): cost of a full scan of the view = HyRowVM x SizeRowVM x fill factor / page size.
C: hasWorkloadFraction of the heuristic x total cost of the workload.
Maximum size of the column in bytes, from its data type (DBMS manual).
The set of tables of the FROM clause of a query (or subquery).
Group REF: any other column referenced by the query block (SELECT, WHERE, HAVING, GROUP BY, ORDER BY).
Group SARG: column in another indexable (sargable) predicate: like, in.
SQL text of the value.
Timestamp of the executed DROP INDEX action.
Group EQ: column in an equality predicate with a value (column = value).
dia_size: indexes with fewer blocks are not rebuilt (default 800 blocks of 8 KB).
Time of a DML statement execution, or time at which the dispatcher executed an action.

SPARQL 1.1 Update that removes the values the rule recomputes from scratch (costs, accumulated benefits, benefit records). The tool executes it before the rules whenever the rule is going to run, so that a new run does not count an execution twice. Kept with the SHACL implementation of the rule (rules.ttl).
SQL text of an aggregate function call of a SELECT or HAVING clause (written by the parser, or by Rule_MV_DefineView for a view).
Status of a real index, computed by Rule_RealIndex_Lifecycle: dbaDecision (CREATE INDEX proposed, not executed yet), created (exists in the database), removed (DROP INDEX executed).
Position of the column in its table.
Column on the right of an atomic expression, when the right operand is a column (join).
Subquery -> statement that contains it.
Position (1, 2, ...) of the atomic expression in the WHERE clause, from left to right.
Timestamp of the executed CREATE INDEX action.
Description or SQL text.
Access structure created, rebuilt or dropped by the action.
«Mediation» administers.
TS-Cost >= C and TS-Weight >= C (InterestingTableSubsets, figure 8).
Column the clause mentions: table.column when the parser knows the table (the alias is replaced by the table name), column alone otherwise.
An execution produces its real plan (from the DBMS) and the hypothetical plan estimated with the hypothetical access structures.
Heuristic that created the access structure.
Name of a table the clause mentions, as written in the SQL (FROM, UPDATE, DELETE FROM, INSERT INTO).
Timestamp of the last executed REINDEX action.
QPL (Oliveira, table 4.3): number of disk pages read by the execution of the query (e.g. EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) in PostgreSQL). Set by the dispatcher on the real plan.
The query can be answered by the view (Weberling, section 2.7): same tables, every column it uses and every aggregate it computes is in the view.
Each Composite Expression has exactly two predicates as operands.
On a heuristic: true, the rules it defines (definesRule) are executed; false, they are skipped. On a rule: false switches off only that rule (no value means enabled).
Column used by the SELECT clause outside aggregate functions (Rule_Column_GroupingReference).
The execution (with its number, timestamp and plans) that produced this record.
Group O: column in ORDER BY, GROUP BY or in a join predicate (column = column of another table, or the same column in a self-join).
Queries with a larger real cost are not considered by the expectation heuristic (5000000 in figure 4.11).
dia_ratio: minimum fragmentation degree (GrF, in %) for an index to be rebuilt (default 50).
C as a fraction of the total cost of the workload (0.10 in Agrawal et al. for SQL Server).
CRC (Oliveira, table 4.3): real execution cost of the query the view was defined from, in its most recent execution.
SQL text of the value on the right of an atomic expression (becomes a Literal).

Accumulated benefit of a real index (Morelli, section 3.2): hasInitialAccumulatedBonus + the RealIndexBonus and IndexUpdateCost records of the executions after its creation (or after its last rebuild). Below -hasEstimatedCreationCost the index is removed (or rebuilt).
Date of a DML statement execution, or date on which the dispatcher executed an action.
Java class of the dispatcher.

Cost estimated by the optimizer for a query or subquery without hypothetical structures (getExecutionCostQuery). Set by the dispatcher; for an executed statement the real plan of the execution is used instead.
Group RANGE: column in a range restriction (between, <, <=, >, >=).
TS-Cost(T): total cost of the queries and subqueries of the workload (one per execution) whose tables include T.
The query or subquery compatible with the view.
sizeTables(T): sum of the page counts of the tables of the subset.
SizeRowVM (Weberling, section 3.1.2): maximum size in bytes of a tuple of the view, the sum of the maximum sizes of its columns.
HypotheticalPlanBenefit: the hypothetical plan accesses the index. RealIndexBonus: the real plan accesses the index.
Tables a view, or the specification of a hypothetical materialized view, is computed from (not in the figures for the specification).
(CRC - QPL) x 100 / CRC (Oliveira, rule 4-4): share of the cost of the query that is processing (CPU) and not reading pages.
Views with a larger estimated creation cost are not materialized by the expectation heuristic (5000000 in figure 4.11).
HyPgVM (Weberling, section 3.1.2): HyRowVM x SizeRowVM / page size, rounded up.
Column on the left of an atomic expression (table.column or column).
Logical connector of a composite expression, as text (and, or).
Bytes assumed for each aggregate column of a view (sum, avg, count...) in SizeRowVM.

hasDate + hasTime (00:00:00 when there is no time), computed by Rule_IndexBenefit_Timestamp. Puts executions and executed actions in order: an execution counts for a real index only between the creation (or the last rebuild) and the removal of the index.
Current number of pages of a real index, measured by the dispatcher in the DBMS (getsize, pgstatindex, pg_class.relpages).
Ri in Morelli, chapter 4: table tuples / index blocks measured right after the creation of the real index (getsize, pgstatindex). Set by the dispatcher.

CCI = 2P + c R log2 R (Salles, 2002, section 4.5.1): read the P pages of the table and write the same number of index pages, plus sorting the R tuples. In plan cost units (one page I/O = 1). Copied to the real index when it is created; -CCI is its elimination threshold.
Column the SELECT clause uses outside aggregate functions (written by the parser).
dia_scans: minimum number of useful scans for an index to be rebuilt (default 2).

QPL used by the expectation heuristic: the pages read by that execution (hasPageReadCount), or the hypothetical pages of the view when the plan does not have them, as in the SWRL rule of Oliveira (figure 4.11).
Rules that are switched on and off together with the heuristic.
X% of the expectation heuristic (rule 4-2): the processing share above which a view is materialized (50 in the experiments of Oliveira, section 6.4.3).
Java package of the dispatcher.
Comparison operator of an atomic expression, as text (=, <, between, like, not in, ...).
V in Morelli, chapter 4: number of executions since the creation of the real index whose real plan used it in a scan (a range predicate on one of its columns: between, <, <=, >, >=).

On a real index (Morelli, section 3.2): accumulated benefit of the hypothetical index divided by the number of executions that used it, fixed when the real index is created. Added to the accumulated bonus each time a real plan uses the index.
In the figure, Index indexes Column. Extended to Index Specification so that hypothetical indexes can point to their columns.
Accumulated benefit of the hypothetical index when it became this real index. Starting value of hasAccumulatedBonus, again after each rebuild.
Number of tuples the plan processed. In the real plan of an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE: the tuples inserted, updated or deleted (r in the update cost of Salles, 2002).
A composite statement also originates what its subqueries originate.
Ordered composition of figure 4; the order is given by the subproperties.
A column that the query block uses in a way that matters for index selection (Lohman et al., in Salles 2002).

Hypothetical index: number of counted executions whose hypothetical plan used it (divides the accumulated benefit to give the bonus). Real index: number of executions since its creation (or its last rebuild) whose real plan used it.
«Mediation» executes.
Signed value of the record, added to the accumulated benefit or bonus of the index.
c in Salles (2002), section 4.5.1: cost of processing one tuple in memory relative to the cost of one page I/O (PostgreSQL: 1%, i.e. 0.01). Used by the creation and update costs of indexes.
Total cost of an execution plan, real or hypothetical.
